name: Harmony Gold Mining Company Limited
moat_justification: A gold miner has no pricing power and Harmony's returns prove it: roic_proxy was negative in four of the last nine years and only exceeds the cost of capital when the gold price rescues it (22.7% FY2024, 37.4% FY2025 at record prices); gross margin swung -15% to +33% on price alone. The 3 rests on scale, the high-grade Mponeng/Hidden Valley cash engines, a net-cash balance sheet, and the CSA/Eva copper pivot — real assets, but a commodity franchise, not a moat.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 16 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

FX_CONVERTED: reporting currency ZAR converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion
USD_TRANSLATIONS_USED: the issuer files its own USD convenience translations alongside its reporting currency; the engine used the filed USD figures

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 20-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Harmony Gold Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025 (filed 2025-10-31), cover page: 'American Depositary Shares (as evidenced by American Depositary Receipts), each representing one ordinary share', trading symbol HMY, New York Stock Exchange) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 0.90 vs 3-yr median 0.61 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
one_liner: South Africa's largest gold producer, moat 3/10 — a price-taker whose owner's earnings are the gold price in disguise; on the normalized FY2023-25 median base ($0.61/share) with gold-price-driven growth recalibrated to volume reality, the weighted IRR is 7.0% (Tier D, IV@15% $5.99 vs $17.12; clears 15% only below $5.99), and FY2026's record print is a gold-price spike, not volume growth — the market is pricing spot gold, not normalized owner's earnings.
moat_for: Scale: South Africa's largest gold producer by volume, ~1.4-1.5 Moz/yr guided for the 11th consecutive year in FY2026
High-grade cornerstone assets: Mponeng (world's deepest, high recovered grades) and Hidden Valley (PNG) generate a disproportionate share of free cash flow
Balance sheet: net cash at FY2025 (net debt -$627M on the engine's USD history) funds the copper pivot without dilution
Copper diversification: CSA mine producing (18,207 t in FY2026) plus Eva Copper approved ($1.55B, first production H2 2028) toward ~100 kt/yr
moat_against: Pure price taker: earnings are the gold price minus AISC; gross margin swung from -15% (FY2018) to +33% (FY2025) on price alone
ROIC through the cycle is mediocre: roic_proxy negative in FY2018-FY2020 and FY2022, spiking to 37% in FY2025 only at record gold prices
Depleting, deep, old South African underground mines: grades and volumes decline without constant life-extension capex; production fell 5% in FY2025 and was flat in FY2026
South Africa operating risk: power supply, labour, safety stoppages (fatal incidents still reported in FY2026 6-Ks), and resource nationalism overhang
Growth is bought, not organic: Mponeng (2020), Eva Copper (2022), MAC Copper/CSA (2025) — reserves replaced by M&A
